paper.title_en: Complexity growth of AdS black holes with higher derivative corrections in presence of string cloud
paper.abstract_en: We investigate the Wilson line sector contribution to holographic complexity for five-dimensional Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet AdS black holes immersed in a static string cloud, working within the complexity equals action framework. The string cloud induces geometric backreaction on the AdS background, while the Gauss-Bonnet (GB) term captures higher derivative curvature corrections from string theory. Following the probe string formalism established in previous works, we compute the time growth rate of the Nambu-Goto worldsheet action for a moving fundamental string over a range of probe velocities, string cloud densities, and GB coupling strengths. This observable isolates nonlocal contributions from heavy Wilson line operators in the dual boundary theory, rather than evaluating the full gravitational action on the Wheeler-DeWitt patch. Our numerical results reveal a nontrivial competition between spacetime backreaction and curvature corrections, governed primarily by the black hole horizon size and probe kinematics. For large black holes, increasing the string cloud density accelerates the Wilson line complexity growth for slowly moving probes but suppresses it at relativistic velocities, producing a characteristic velocity dependent crossover. Small black holes exhibit no such crossover, with complexity rising monotonically with cloud density for all probe speeds. GB curvature corrections reduce the probe string complexity growth across all parameter choices, with much stronger suppression acting on small black holes due to their enhanced near horizon curvature. Beyond critical values of the GB coupling and cloud density, thermodynamically unstable small black hole solutions disappear, and the single surviving stable black hole recovers the dynamical signatures of large black hole geometries. Geometric analysis shows that slowly moving strings access deeper bulk regions and amplify complexity, while relativistic probes remain confined near the horizon and yield lower complexity growth. This work demonstrates that the horizon scale controls the interplay between background geometric deformations and the Wilson line sector of holographic complexity in strongly coupled conformal theories.
